Evaluation before optimisation

“Better” becomes useful when the room agrees what it means

For Priya, a useful research brief should…

  • answer the research question using only the supplied excerpts
  • label which source supports each finding
  • separate evidence from interpretation
  • identify disagreements, limitations and missing evidence
  • suggest searches without inventing papers or citations
  • leave the assessed argument and prose with Priya
If we cannot describe success, we cannot judge whether a prompt change helped.

02
Context engineering

What should the model see while it works?

Context engineering means choosing and maintaining the information available at each step, rather than placing every possible document into one prompt.

The information available on this turn

What belongs in the working context at this step?

InstructionsThe job, boundaries and expected behaviour.
Student informationDeadlines, availability and progress that matter now.
Conversation historyEarlier decisions that still affect the task.
Retrieved materialRelevant passages brought in when needed.
Tool resultsCurrent information returned by the system.

The useful context changes as the work changes.

Choose → use → update → remove

Deadline triage · audience activity

Which information belongs on Maya’s desk right now?

Working context
Signal, not volume

More material can make the important material harder to see

Focused

Current deadlines

Available hours

Task progress

versus

Overloaded

Relevant + stale + duplicated + conflicting + enormous

Aim for the smallest working context that performs reliably, then retrieve more when the task asks for it.

Tools and agent loops

What changes when the model can check the world?

For Noah’s group, a useful answer depends on room availability that is not sitting in the prompt.

A durable mental model

An agent is a model choosing actions in a feedback loop

Goal
Organise a group meeting
→
Model chooses
What is missing?
→
Tool request
Find a suitable room
Result returns to context ↺

The model requests a structured action. The surrounding application executes it and returns an observable result.

Reading what happened

    It recognised that availability was missing.

The trace shows observable events, never hidden chain-of-thought.

Designing the interface

A tool description is a handover to a new team member

Hard to use
search(x)

Search what? What is x? What comes back?

Clear enough to choose
find_study_room(
  date, time, group_size,
  accessibility_required
)

Returns matching rooms or an explicit no-match result.

Same tools, different instructions

Why did three coordinators behave differently?

Called everything

It treated tool availability as a checklist.

Only wrote advice

It never used the capabilities needed to move the task forward.

Checked what mattered

It used the minimum information and actions needed for the group’s goal.

Under the hood

The loop is small; deciding when to stop is the interesting part

while not finished:
    response = model(context, tools)
    if response.requests_tool:
        result = execute_tool()
        context += result
    else:
        finished = True
model→action→result↺

Audience classification

Who controls the next step?

A workflow follows a predetermined path. An agent lets the model choose its process and tool use.
Architecture choice

Use the least complicated system that works reliably

One promptFixed workflowSingle agentSeveral agents

Formatting weekly notes? A workflow is enough.

Coordinating calendars and rooms after failures? A single agent may earn its complexity.

Running one calculation? Do not build a team of agents.

When the room service fails

A useful agent treats failure as new information

Waiting for Noah

Pause before consequential, expensive, irreversible or externally visible actions.

Knowledge and orchestration

How should Priya work across notes, readings and a rubric?

The aim is to help her find evidence, test an argument and revise—without outsourcing the assessed thinking.

Before adding more agents

Separate responsibilities only when the work genuinely decomposes

Search readingsCompare sourcesMap the rubricChallenge the argumentCreate revision questionsTrack citations

Different prompts, tools, context and goals can create useful specialists. More names in boxes do not.

Cost and coordination

Did the extra calls produce a better learning outcome?

One call is enough

Turn these ten definitions into a two-column revision table.

Decomposition may help

Compare evidence from several readings, map it to rubric criteria and test Priya’s proposed argument for unsupported claims.

More agents mean more latency, cost, coordination and places to fail.
Retrieval

The model does not automatically know Priya’s unit materials

General knowledge

It may understand common essay structures and study techniques.

Private or current knowledge

It does not know the latest unit outline, lecture notes, rubric or Priya’s draft unless the system supplies them.

question→retrieve→relevant passages→answer with sources
Interactive retrieval

Which document deserves a place in the working context?

assessment_policy.txt

Extension requests must be submitted before the published deadline unless exceptional circumstances prevent this.

unit_outline.txt

The essay rubric rewards a defensible argument, appropriate evidence and accurate citation.

room_rules.txt

Study rooms must remain within capacity and accessible routes must stay clear.

Retrieved text should be cited and treated as evidence, not permission to invent missing policy.
